findings.title: text.ipynb: Wikipedia path is dead for everyone (wikipedia 1.4.0 UA blocked by Wikimedia); bare except silently swaps in 4-sentence toy text that contradicts the narration
findings.description: Cells 4/10 fetch pages with the unmaintained `wikipedia` 1.4.0 package. Wikimedia now blocks that package's shared User-Agent ('wikipedia (https://github.com/goldsmith/Wikipedia/)'): the API returns a plain-text block page, and the package dies with requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError. The tutorial's bare `except:` then silently substitutes 1-2 sentence fallback strings, so every user (and the shipped notebook itself -- its stored cell 6 output is the 39-char fallback chunk) runs the whole 'Visualizing text' section on toy text. The narration still promises real content: 'Below is a snippet of some of the text from the dog wikipedia page ... words related to dog like wolf and carnivore appear' (the displayed 39-char chunk contains neither claim), and 'the 5 chunks of text from the dog/cat wiki pages cluster together' (in the actual figure the red/cyan points intermix; see text_cell08_out0.png). Fix options: fetch with a descriptive UA via requests directly (verified working: curl -A 'HyperToolsAudit/1.0 (email)' succeeds, title 'Dog', length 192157), vendor the two pages as a hosted dataset, or rewrite the narration for the fallback text; and replace `except:` with a printed notice so the substitution is never silent.
findings.expected: Wikipedia page content downloads (the tutorial narrates real dog/cat/basketball wiki text), or at minimum a visible notice that fallback text is in use
findings.actual: requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) -- underlying API response (curl with the package's UA): 'You are making too many requests to the API.\nPlease follow the best practices at <https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_APIs/Rate_limits>.' Tutorial cell 6 stored output: 'Dogs are domesticated mammals, not nat'

findings.title: text.ipynb cells 12-22: narration describes NIPS/Wikipedia/SOTUS dataset plots (dots colored+labeled by president, TSNE, HDBSCAN) but the code plots 4-16 generic sentences as bare red interpolated lines
findings.description: Cell 12 md: 'The next example is a dataset of all NIPS papers published from 1987 ... This example dataset can be loaded using the code below' -- the code creates 4 hardcoded sentences and never loads anything. Cell 14 md: 'we will plot a collection of wikipedia pages ... We will reduce the dimensionality of the data with TSNE, and then discover cluster with the HDBSCAN algorithm' -- the code uses 4 sample sentences with default PCA and no clustering. Cell 16 md: 'we will plot each state of the union address from 1989 to present. The dots are colored and labeled by president ... points generally seem to cluster by president ... democrats mostly on the left and republicans mostly on the right' -- the code plots 16 generic sentences with NO fmt/hue/labels, so the figure is a single unlabeled red line (text_cell17_out0.png), with no dots, no colors, no presidents. Cells 13/15/19/21 likewise render discrete documents as one connected interpolated red line, which is meaningless for unordered documents. Every claimed insight in this half of the tutorial is unverifiable from what the code shows. Fix: either load the real hosted 'nips'/'sotus' data (hyp.load) with hue/labels matching the prose, or rewrite the prose for the sample sentences and pass 'o' + hue so figures show grouped dots.
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
sample_sotus = ['My fellow Americans, the state of our union is strong.']*1 + ['...15 more generic sentences...']
fig = hyp.plot(sample_sotus, size=[10,8])  # exact cell 17 form: no fmt, no hue -> single red line
findings.expected: Dots colored and labeled by president, matching the markdown claims (or markdown matching the sample-sentence reality)
findings.actual: Figures are single-color connected interpolated lines with no labels/legend (text_cell17_out0.png, text_cell13_out0.png, text_cell19_out0.png, text_cell21_out0.png); no dataset is loaded in any of these cells

findings.title: text.ipynb cells 19 and 21 display each figure twice (unassigned hyp.plot(...) expression -> execute_result + inline display_data)
findings.description: Cells 19 and 21 call `hyp.plot(...)` without assigning the returned Figure. Under %matplotlib inline the figure is emitted once by the inline display hook (display_data) and again as the cell's execute_result (the Figure's rich repr), so readers of the rendered tutorial see the identical image twice back-to-back. Verified in BOTH the shipped notebook (tracked cell 19 outputs: stream + execute_result[image/png] + display_data[image/png]) and a fresh execution (cells 19/21 each produced two byte-identical PNGs). Every other plotting cell in the notebook uses `fig = hyp.plot(...)` and displays once. Fix: assign to fig (or add a trailing semicolon) in cells 19/21.
findings.repro: jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute docs/tutorials/text.ipynb  # then inspect cells 19/21: two identical image/png outputs each
findings.actual: tracked cell 19: 3 outputs -> [('stream', []), ('execute_result', ['image/png', 'text/plain']), ('display_data', ['image/png', 'text/plain'])]; fresh run: text_cell19_out0.png == text_cell19_out1.png (65004 bytes each)

findings.title: cluster='HDBSCAN' leaks a sklearn FutureWarning ('default value of copy will change ... in 1.10') into user-facing output, including cluster.ipynb cell 20
findings.description: hypertools constructs sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN without pinning the `copy` parameter, so under scikit-learn 1.8 every HDBSCAN fit prints 'FutureWarning: The default value of `copy` will change from False to True in 1.10. Explicitly set a value for `copy` to silence this warning.' The warning appears as red stderr in the rendered cluster tutorial (cell 20) and in any user script using cluster='HDBSCAN' (modern_sklearn_dynamics.ipynb only avoids it via warnings.filterwarnings('ignore'), which hides ALL warnings -- itself a heavy hammer). Beyond the noise, the flagged default is changing under hypertools' feet in sklearn 1.10 (copy False -> True), so behavior/performance should be pinned deliberately in the Clusterer registry defaults.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.cluster(np.random.randn(100,3), cluster='HDBSCAN')
findings.expected: No FutureWarning in tutorial/user output; copy= pinned explicitly where HDBSCAN is constructed
findings.actual: stream/stderr in executed cluster.ipynb cell 20: '/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sklearn/cluster/_hdbscan/hdbscan.py:722: FutureWarning: The default value of `copy` will change from False to True in 1.10. Explicitly set a value for `copy` to silence this warning.'

findings.title: cluster.ipynb markdown/code errors: 'arrray', 'we have note specified' (x2), figure titled 'HCBSCAN clustering', cell-19 text claims n_clusters=10 is passed but the code omits it, supported-model list incomplete
findings.description: (1) Cell 2 md: 'clustering analysis on the data (an arrray, dataframe, or list)' -- typo. (2) Cells 11 and 16 md: 'since we have note specified' -- typo, twice. (3) Cell 21 code titles the second figure 'HCBSCAN clustering' (should be HDBSCAN); the typo is baked into the rendered figure (cluster_cell21_out1.png). (4) Cell 19 md: 'we specify both the clustering model (HDBSCAN) and the number of clusters (10)' but cell 20 runs hyp.cluster(mushrooms, cluster='HDBSCAN') with no n_clusters -- and n_clusters would be ignored for HDBSCAN anyway per the docstring, so the sentence teaches a wrong mental model. (5) Cell 2 md lists only 7 supported algorithms; the actual registry has 15 (adds MeanShift, DBSCAN, OPTICS, AffinityPropagation + mixtures GaussianMixture, BayesianGaussianMixture, LatentDirichletAllocation, NMF -- enumerated verbatim by the unknown-name error message).

findings.title: FeatureAgglomeration is advertised as a clustering model returning 'one label per observation' but actually labels FEATURES; via plot() it crashes with a cryptic sklearn tree error
findings.description: hyp.cluster's docstring promises 'a list of cluster labels (one per observation)' and both the docstring and cluster.ipynb cell 2 list FeatureAgglomeration among supported models with no caveat. FeatureAgglomeration clusters COLUMNS: hyp.cluster(randn(30,4), cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', n_clusters=2) returns 4 labels for 30 observations. Passed to plot (where labels become hue), it crashes deep in sklearn: 'ValueError: Cannot extract more clusters than samples: 5 clusters were given for a tree with 3 leaves.' (plot reduces to 3 columns first, then asks for 5 feature-clusters of 3 features). Either document the per-feature semantics prominently (and block/adapt it in plot with a clear message), or drop it from the advertised cluster list.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
labels = hyp.cluster(np.random.randn(30, 4), cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', n_clusters=2)
print(len(labels))  # 4, not 30
hyp.plot(np.random.randn(30, 4), '.', cluster='FeatureAgglomeration')  # crashes
findings.expected: Per the docstring, one label per observation (30), or a clear error/doc caveat explaining FeatureAgglomeration labels features
findings.actual: len(labels) == 4 for a (30,4) input; plot raises 'ValueError: Cannot extract more clusters than samples: 5 clusters were given for a tree with 3 leaves.'

findings.title: normalize.ipynb: dangling 'Or, to specify a different normalization...' with no preceding default example; ungrammatical intro; unseeded RNG makes shipped outputs irreproducible
findings.description: (1) Cell 10 heading 'Normalizing (Specified Cols or Rows)' is immediately followed by cell 11 'Or, to specify a different normalization, pass one of the following arguments...' -- the 'Or' refers to a default-usage example that does not exist in the notebook (the pre-1.0 tutorial had a 'normalize with defaults' section first). Readers meet an alternative before any primary usage. (2) Cell 2: 'The `normalize` is a helper function to z-score your data' -- grammar. (3) Cell 7 draws data with np.random.* and no seed, so every execution (and the shipped figures) differ run-to-run; the other three audited notebooks that need determinism use random_state/seeded generators.
findings.expected: A default-usage example before the 'Or...' alternative, grammatical intro, and a seeded RNG for reproducible tutorial figures

findings.title: hyp.normalize invalid-mode error is an AssertionError naming a nonexistent parameter 'scale_type'
findings.description: Passing a bad mode string raises 'AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' Problems: (a) the parameter is named `normalize`, not `scale_type` (a pre-1.0 relic), so users grep for a kwarg that does not exist; (b) it is an assert, so running under `python -O` skips validation entirely and the bad value flows into Normalizer.transform (which raises its own, correctly-worded ValueError: "normalize must be 'across', 'within', or 'row'; got ..." -- the two messages also disagree); (c) 'none' in the message means the Python literals False/None, which a plain-string reading obscures. Replace the assert with a ValueError mirroring Normalizer.transform's wording.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.normalize([np.random.randn(10, 3)], normalize='blah')
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize must be 'across', 'within', 'row', False, None, or a fitted Normalizer; got 'blah'
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: normalize docstring and tutorial claim 'If the input was a list, a list is returned' / 'output type same as input type' -- false for one-element lists
findings.description: hyp.normalize([single_array]) returns a bare ndarray, not a 1-element list: the return branch is `if internal or len(normalized_x) > 1: result = normalized_x else: result = normalized_x[0]`, which unwraps by ELEMENT COUNT rather than by input type. The docstring Returns section says 'If the input was a list, a list is returned. Otherwise, an array is returned', and normalize.ipynb cell 2 says 'returns an array or list of arrays where the columns or rows are z-scored (output type same as input type)'. Code written generically over lists of datasets (e.g. `[hyp.normalize(group)[0] for group in groups]`) silently indexes rows of the array when a group has one dataset. Either preserve list-in/list-out or document the single-element unwrap explicitly.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
out = hyp.normalize([np.random.randn(60, 4)])
print(type(out))  # <class 'numpy.ndarray'>, docstring promises list
findings.expected: list of length 1 (per docstring), or a docstring documenting the unwrap

findings.title: Misspelled corpus name is silently treated as a literal one-document training corpus (garbage embeddings, no warning)
findings.description: text2mat only special-cases corpus in ('wiki','nips','sotus'); any OTHER string falls through `corpus = np.array([corpus])` and the semantic model is fit on the literal string as a single document. hyp.plot(docs, corpus='wiki ') or corpus='Wiki' or corpus='bogus-name' therefore produces confidently-wrong topic vectors ((2,20) matrix from a vocabulary of the typo itself) with no error or warning. text.ipynb cell 20 explicitly teaches "set corpus='nips'", making name typos likely. Fix: warn (or raise) when corpus is a plain string that is not a hosted-corpus name -- a single string is almost never a meaningful corpus.
findings.repro:
import warnings, hypertools as hyp
m = hyp.tools.format_data(['some document to embed', 'another document here'], corpus='bogus-name')
print([x.shape for x in m])  # [(2, 20)] -- LDA fit on the literal string 'bogus-name'
findings.expected: ValueError or at least a UserWarning ('corpus 'bogus-name' is not one of wiki/nips/sotus; treating it as a 1-document corpus')
findings.actual: Silent success: bogus corpus result shape: [(2, 20)]

findings.title: Mixed text+numeric input with mismatched sample counts fails with a raw numpy vstack error that never mentions text/alignment
findings.description: format_data documents mixed lists ('x : numpy array, dataframe, string or (mixed) list') and auto-aligns text+numeric when sample counts match (verified working: [3 docs, (3,4) array] -> [(3,50),(3,50)] with a clear UserWarning). But when counts do NOT match -- [2 docs, (5,3) array] -- the vectorized (2,50) text and (5,3) array flow into a bare np.vstack and the user gets 'ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 50 and the array at index 1 has size 3', with no hint that the issue is text/numeric sample-count mismatch or that same-count inputs would be hyperaligned. Raise a targeted message from format_data instead.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.plot([['text one', 'text two'], np.random.randn(5, 3)], 'o')
findings.expected: Error naming the real problem, e.g. 'mixed text (2 samples) and numeric (5 samples) datasets must have the same number of samples to be aligned to a common space'

findings.title: Continuous hue uses the cyclic hls palette, so the FIRST and LAST timepoints get nearly the same red -- weakening the tutorial claim that 'color traces the passage of time'
findings.description: modern_sklearn_dynamics cell 9 md: 'Passing a continuous array as hue draws the trajectory as a multicolored line, so color traces the passage of time.' The multicolored line is real and the mapping is a single monotonic sweep (verified: 199 unique segment colors on a 200-point ramp, hls hue angle 0.01 -> 0.255 -> 0.505 -> 0.75 -> 0.0, 99.5% increasing). But hls is a CYCLIC palette: the endpoint wraps back to the start hue, so t=0 and t=T are both red-ish and cannot be told apart -- on the Lorenz attractor the trajectory's beginning and end look the same. A perceptually-ordered non-cyclic default (e.g. viridis) for continuous hue, or a sentence in the tutorial acknowledging the wrap, would make time uniquely readable.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp, matplotlib.colors as mc
t = np.linspace(0, 1, 200); ramp = np.column_stack([t, 0*t, 0*t])
fig = hyp.plot(ramp, hue=np.arange(200.)); fig.canvas.draw()
big = max(fig.axes[0].collections, key=lambda c: len(c.get_segments()))
h = mc.rgb_to_hsv(np.asarray(big.get_colors())[:, :3])[:, 0]
print(h[0], h[-1])  # ~0.01 vs ~0.0 -- same hue at both ends
findings.expected: Distinct colors for earliest vs latest timepoints so time maps uniquely to color
findings.actual: hue angle start/25%/50%/75%/end: [0.01, 0.255, 0.505, 0.75, 0.0] -- endpoints visually identical red
